    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1058 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Everything but the Plane: Here’s How One Brand Is Bringing Glamour Back to Travel

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that imagine a trip to the airport with no lines.
    • According to recent reports, airlines can solve only so many problems.
    • According to recent reports, the company has locations in Atlanta, Dallas Fort Worth, Miami, and Los Angeles, and the next order of business is expansion to the airports its clients use most—business hubs, mostly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that imagine a trip to the airport with no lines. No lines to check in, to drop your bag, to be told your first-class ticket is the wrong first-class ticket for the first-class lounge. Now add to that no interpersonal friction. There are no snappy desk workers, no turbo TSA employees, and no graveyard-shift customs agents that give you grief.

    According to recent reports, airlines can solve only so many problems. These are terminal problems. PS, a Los Angeles–based manufacturer operating its own luxury private terminals, is solving them. The goal is to get you as close to the charter experience as possible, all while still flying commercial. If you ask around or sit in the common areas and eavesdrop long enough, you’ll likely hear something along the lines of “I usually fly private, but when I don’t, this is what I use.”.

    According to recent reports, the company has locations in Atlanta, Dallas Fort Worth, Miami, and Los Angeles, and the next order of business is expansion to the airports its clients use most—business hubs, mostly. But it started at LAX in 2017, and that’s the perfect airport for something like this. The horseshoe design and the traffic it creates, the small terminals, and the paparazzi culture do not cater to the A-list and executive frequent fliers that use it as a home airport. PS offers a way around that with on-tarmac connection from your flight to its terminal and vice versa. A chauffeur pulls you straight off the jet bridge and into a luxury fleet vehicle; that partnership is currently with BMW. If you don’t have any checked luggage, that 7 Series can (for an additional price) drive you straight to your destination within 35 miles of the airport. So if you are sitting in row 1 of first class, that’s about 50 steps between you and the i7 that takes you to your hotel. Or it can take you back to the PS terminal, which is not a lounge but acts as an über-private lounge experience.

    In a recent development, it ain’t cheap: $1,300 per head one-way for the Salon (a shared bar area), $4,950 for a private suite (essentially an airport hotel room with butler and spa service; this price is all-inclusive), and $1,650 for that PS Direct drive-you-straight-home service. There are discounts and perks if you opt for yearly membership, but this is all on top of your ticket, folks.

    And it can lean comically luxurious, with Champagne and caviar offered every time you enter—like before my 8:00 a.m. departure, to which I’m not opposed but which caught me a little off guard. There’s the jet-set marketing—tagline: The “back door” to the airport—and meant-for-the-timeline branded cocktail napkins: “You’ve arrived.”.

    Sources indicate that but once you accept that PS could not afford to excuse itself from the flex-driven airport exclusivity economy, you can really admire its hospitality-inspired finishes. Its raison d’être is to get you through the airport with as little friction as possible, but it stands out in its commitment to hospitality within those confines.

    It has been revealed that for example, interior design and artwork are curated. The centerpiece artworks of each location are done in collaboration with local artists, made to fit the location they are in. The crown jewel thus far is in Miami, where PS took over the old Pan Am headquarters and flight-training academy. The mid-century building is a Miami landmark, with geometric thermal walls acting as the facades and this pinkish sandy and limestone-heavy concrete throughout. Argentinian-born ceramicist Nina Surel matched this with tile-work water features and a ceramic mural at the center of the property. Design like this, small and mostly unnoticed in the grand scheme of things, is what turns your mind back to a golden age of travel. It’s not credit card points and moneymaking schemes—though, actually, you can buy any of the non-centerpiece artworks—just beauty for the sake of beauty.

    Sources indicate that on top of that, the food and beverage program is considered and regional. The blue-corn cornbread with honey and a ricotta spread that chef Kelsey Kirwin (chefs’ names are on the menus, an indication of the atmosphere) is making at the DFW location overtook my mother’s as my all-time favorite. I would consider the signature PS martini—with (guess what) caviar-stuffed olives—worthy of a place on any hot substantial-city cocktail menu. And all the coffees, snacks, and water options are head and shoulders above those of both the general-population terminals and the litany of airport lounges within them.

    Recent findings suggest that as far as service, yes, an agent handles your party’s check-in and keeps you abreast of delays so you don’t have to open an app—but that’s to be expected. It’s more in the interim. Servers don’t hover, they listen, and they’re backed by an extensive behind-the-scenes operation: Mention that you prefer coffee, not bubbles, before a morning flight? A note is made on your profile for the next time you visit. Only ever ask for sparkling water when you fly out of LAX? They’ll know that in Atlanta. The entire operation seems to run on Guidara’s Unreasonable Hospitality, the same way all modern restaurants do. If you’re leaving Miami and mention to a business partner that you forgot to try a Cubano (on menu) and a cafecito (off menu), both will likely be delivered to your table, compliments of the house.

    But every time I start to get wowed by the service details, I remember the price point and the level of clientele. That should be expected.

    Sources indicate that standard terminals are air-side, post-security, where everything (even a fancy and expensive airline lounge) is working within those confines. Since PS operates land-side, with security the last stage of the terminal experience, it has the flexibility to be more hospitable to guests. For example, if you book a private suite, you can fly in, use it for a business meeting, and fly out. Or your parents can accompany the family to departure, hang out in the suite, and squeeze every last second with the grandkids out of your visit. It is an airport experience actually designed around the ways we interact and what matters to us when we travel. That, more than the Champagne and caviar, is the definition of luxury.

    #123618. How to Do a Chrome Manicure Over Regular Nail Polish If You’re Feeling Really Brave

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1509 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

    How to Do a Chrome Manicure Over Regular Nail Polish If You’re Feeling Really Brave

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
    • Industry observers note that there are, in my view, four types of DIY nail art: Manicures that are as easy to do as they look, designs looks complicated but are actually pretty simple, motifs that are exactly as hard as they look, and nail art that seems like it should be a breeze but are actually a pain in the butt.
    • In fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

    Industry observers note that there are, in my view, four types of DIY nail art: Manicures that are as easy to do as they look, designs looks complicated but are actually pretty simple, motifs that are exactly as hard as they look, and nail art that seems like it should be a breeze but are actually a pain in the butt. Chrome manicures fall into that last category, especially if you’re trying to layer the metallic powder over regular polish.

    In fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try. “In my experience, improvising with loose chrome pigment over regular polish can become a long, tedious process with inconsistent results,” says nail artist Max Estrada. “A manicure should be a little luxury, not an endurance examination.”.

    It’s a fair warning: Chrome definitely works best with gel, and it’s going to take a lot of trial and error to get that mirror-like shine on top of regular polish. But there are lots of legit reasons that some people avoid gel in their at-home manicure station (allergies... you have to buy a whole UV setup... it’s tedious to remove...), and those people might still want to try the chocolate chrome look so beloved by Hailey Bieber right now. (Also, some of us are just artistic masochists who find it reasonable that the cost of creative satisfaction would be some failed attempts and frustrated tears.).

    So, if you’re feeling up for the challenge—and have a lot of time to wait for your polish to dry completely—here are some tips for getting a chrome manicure with regular polish. (Results absolutely not guaranteed!).

    While you can use any regular polish you’d like as your base color for this, there are a few different techniques that can work for a chrome finish, indicates Jackie of @jackie.shades. However, she’s gotten so good at applying chrome over regular polish people on the internet are calling her approach “The Jackie Method,” so I’m going to stick with that. For that method, you’ll need:.

    According to recent reports, chrome is not very forgiving of lumps and bumps, so you’ll need to do some careful nail prep before you get started. In addition to the usual filing, hangnail trimming, and cuticle pushing, Jackie recommends a smoothing base coat like Halo Taco Smoothing Base or What’s Up Nails Hideaway Ridge to give you a smooth base to start on.

    As far as your station goes, Jackie emphasizes that chrome is messy. “Make sure you turn off any fans, work on a silicone mat or paper towel, try not to flick any dust into the air, and wear a face mask,” she notes. That last point is because chrome powder is a super fine dust—you don’t want to breathe that in.

    This is the method Jackie has found works best for her nails (and others on Instagram who’ve tried it say it works great for them too) but she leads with a massive disclaimer that everyone is different. “Some products work for some and not for others,” Jackie notes. “If something doesn’t work out, just keep experimenting.”.

    Sources indicate that after your nails are prepped, apply thin layers of your color polish of choice. Keeping them thin is notable, Jackie notes, since this prevents air bubbles that will be noticeable once you add the chrome powder. Also, thin layers dry more quickly.

    It has been revealed that having completely dry polish is one of the biggest keys to success for this look. “The base polish should be dry enough that if you press on your nail plate with your finger, it doesn’t leave any dents,” Jackie says. In my experience, this can take hours with some polish (I told you this wasn’t some easy breezy DIY mani). If you want to be really safe, you could even paint the base color on the night and finish the next steps the following day.

    In a recent development, next, you’ll be creating the tacky base for the chrome to stick to. While you can use any quick dry top coat here, Jackie recommends a 3-free (meaning it’s free of toluene, formaldehyde, and dibutyl phthalate) formula for ease. “ Toluene can sometimes cause certain nail polish colors to ‘bleed’ or ‘run’ so this just helps to avoid any unnecessary cleanup,” she claims.

    Again, you’ll need to let this layer dry until you don’t get any dents if you press into it. Luckily, this usually takes less than five minutes with a quick dry. “I cannot emphasize enough the importance of letting each layer dry,” Jackie indicates. “Most problems that come up (polish wrinkling, bubbles, weird texture, chrome looking cloudy etc.) are because one of the layers wasn't fully dry.”.

    In a recent development, finally, the fun part. Jackie uses her finger to apply the chrome (but only on regular polish—doing so on gel could lead to skin irritation) but you can also use an eyeshadow sponge or cosmetic wedge.

    It has been revealed that to apply, tap your tool of choice into the chrome powder pot and gently wipe it onto the nail. Then, use the tool to buff the chrome into your nail until it creates a smooth, metallic finish. Once you’re happy with how it looks, use a significant fluffy brush to brush away the excess.

    Recent findings suggest that once the chrome is applied, wait at least another 15 minutes to ensure the top coat underneath it is truly, 100% dry. Then, Jackie indicates to swipe a 240 grit buffer block along the free edge of your nail to remove any excess chrome powder. “Now, brush off any additional excess and use a clean cosmetic wedge to gently wipe and tap over the nail to get any leftover loose chrome,” she says.

    After lots of trial and error, Jackie found that the alcohol-based top coat DRK Seal Glaze “keeps the mirror shine and stays on nails longer than a water-based top coat.” You’ll want to apply two coats of it at this point, waiting about 10 minutes (or until the cloudiness turns clear) in between each coat. Make sure you’re applying thin coats that go all the way to the edges of your nails—if you miss any spots, those areas could turn glittery. Then, wait at least 30 minutes for the glaze to dry completely.

    Recent findings suggest that after everything is completely dry, you’ll want to finish with the same top coat you applied before the chrome powder. Even on gel polish chrome is notoriously prone to chipping, but Jackie indicates this glaze + top coat combo helps with longevity, especially if you use the top coat to wrap the tip of your nail.

    Unlike with gels, removal is way easier than applying here: Jackie notes you can take this off just like you would any other regular polish manicure.

    If all of this is making your head spin, Estrada notes that there are some chrome-effect regular polishes that can get pretty close to this mirror-like finish. “A chrome-effect lacquer is an alternative finish, not a promise that every bottle will reproduce the same mirror effect as a professional pigment-and-gel system,” he indicates. “The vital thing is to choose the right product for the finish you want, rather than expect an improvised combination to perform identically.” Sally Hansen and Essie, both sell chrome-effect polishes, though they do look more glittery than a true chrome finish. There’s no shame in this game, Estrada says: “There’s nothing wrong with taking the more straightforward route.”.

    #123616. How the Holy Is Revered and Corrupted in The Body

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (923 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

    How the Holy Is Revered and Corrupted in The Body

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I wanted nothing more than to see the Holy Spirit.
    • Industry observers note that I soon let go of the institutionalized beliefs.
    • Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell thrust the audience into an age of Razor flip phones, AOL instant messaging, and Juicy Couture tracksuits, all set to a 2000s soundtrack featuring Kylie Minogue and No Doubt.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I wanted nothing more than to see the Holy Spirit. One day after church, my grandfather described the moment he first believed was witnessing the Holy Spirit: a soothing, cleansing sensation in which God, in some way, possessed and reassured your mind. Divine intervention felt attainable for a moment. At first, I, too, hoped to discover serenity, an especially enticing thought since my parents were far less religious. But over time, that belief twisted in my preteen mind, instilling instead a fear that every misstep might damn me. To be viewed unfavorably by God—as a kid—is a terrifying thought. And it lingers.

    Industry observers note that I soon let go of the institutionalized beliefs. Yet, a longing to believe in something greater—especially when facing the unknown—never fully left me. I still desired to find spiritual ground, one free from this all-consuming, stress-fueling shame. This friction between spiritual surrender and self-actualization is the beating heart of Quinn Shephard’s The Body. Beneath a relentless downpour of religious guilt and an insatiable appetite for forgiveness, the students at St. Mark’s Catholic High School battle their inner demons as they discern what they want for themselves versus what the world expects of them.

    Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell thrust the audience into an age of Razor flip phones, AOL instant messaging, and Juicy Couture tracksuits, all set to a 2000s soundtrack featuring Kylie Minogue and No Doubt. Its barbed-edged storytelling draws comparisons to Cruel Intentions and Pretty Little Liars, with a bewitching touch of Jennifer’s Body or The Crucible. Here, girl teenagedom traverses suppressed sapphic love and the systemic weaponization of religious guilt—an incisive critique biting enough to solicit a petition with over 120,000 people pushing to cancel it. This coming-of-age series emerges from the dual nature of what we hold sacred: its capacity for reverence and its vulnerability to corruption.

    According to recent reports, catholic school scares me. Teenagers scare me more, especially Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros), the hyper-religious, manipulative student at the heart of the story. At first, The Body introduces us to Lisbeth as the quintessential “weird kid,” socially ostracized because of her eyebrow-less face and her freakishly religious family. (She evokes Carrie in Carrie.) But as The Body unfolds, Lisbeth pulls—or rather, tugs—at the web of guilt ensnaring the school’s dance team, the Lions, concerning the near-death of their new teammate, Grace (Sofia Wylie). Grace fell into a coma shortly after the girls pretended to sacrifice her at a Halloween party, popping ecstasy pills they referred to as the “body of Satan.” This hazing ritual is all in good fun until Grace’s heart actually stops … if only briefly.

    Industry observers note that the aftermath casts a shadow of guilt over everything—especially for Anya (Kristina Bogic), queen bee and dance team captain, who moved Grace’s unconscious body back to her bedroom with Lisbeth’s help. Soon after, Anya begins to see visions of Grace in her dreams. The moment she confesses this to the group, the other girls start confirming visions of their comatose friend. This uncanny groupthink preys on the girls with something to hide, who carry shame with them wherever they go. Anya, for instance, feels deep contrition for her romantic feelings for her best friend Elise (Sarah Boustany), whereas Elise more boldly embraces her queer sexuality. Elise faces the world with a steady confidence, shielding her from spiritual panic—and its subsequent manipulation.

    It has been revealed that the same isn’t true for most of her teammates, all of whom seek solace in the intangible, in God and the Holy Spirit, in the saintly visions of Grace. Grace then becomes a symbol of the sacred, a story that inspires people and therefore can be corrupted to control others. The girls’ desperate need for forgiveness makes them vulnerable to Lisbeth’s manipulation. When the team goes on a getaway together, they take hallucinogenic mushrooms before deciding that they must purge evil spirits from Grace by way of an exorcism (led by Lisbeth, of course). Lisbeth controls this ritual, forcing each girl to confess their sins. (She already knows them all after reading all their private messages.) Her feigned omniscience incites hysteria among the girls.

    Shame clouds nearly all the girls’ minds. Maddie (Shirley Chen) wrestles with an eating disorder, some girls admit to premarital sex or impure thoughts, and Lisbeth attempts to squeeze out a confession from Elise about her feelings for Anya. The Body runs the gamut of teenage girlhood, but Shephard distills these insecurities into a single critique of control: how the holy—the fear of God—can exploit people, corrupt what we see, and shape what we believe. In episode 6, “Star Quality,” mass hysteria breaks out in the town, with people associated with the church now believing to see visions and revere Grace as a saintly figure. It’s driven by an innate desire to be seen—to see something—and a desperate desire to be part of something larger.

    In a recent development, this same desire, to witness something collectively transcendent, forged the foundation of my spiritual beliefs. It also scared me enough to run from them. A connection to God came with fear of hellfire and the shame of sin. In this way, forgiveness felt like something I received out of desperation, rather than salvation. The Body studies the dangers of this unmitigated belief, of a doctrine designed to parse out the unknown. But by whose authority? Shephard’s story reminds us that the storyteller—the pastor or the manipulative teenage girl—controls the things we see and the things we may believe.

    Survey Finds 84% of Organizations Reported at Least One AI-Related Incident in the Past Year

    📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Companies are running into problems as they give artificial intelligence more control over critical business applications, with 84% reporting at least one AI-related incident in the past year, according to a new survey from identity security firm Delinea.
    • It has been revealed that the company's 2026 Application Access Governance report found that some organizations have experienced incorrect financial transactions and AI actions they couldn't trace or explain.
    • The findings are based on an independent survey of 1,000 senior finance and finance technology leaders in the United States and United Kingdom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Companies are running into problems as they give artificial intelligence more control over critical business applications, with 84% reporting at least one AI-related incident in the past year, according to a new survey from identity security firm Delinea.

    It has been revealed that the company's 2026 Application Access Governance report found that some organizations have experienced incorrect financial transactions and AI actions they couldn't trace or explain. The findings raise concerns about whether enterprises have enough oversight of AI systems that can make decisions and take actions on their own.

    The findings are based on an independent survey of 1,000 senior finance and finance technology leaders in the United States and United Kingdom. The AI-specific analysis included 879 respondents whose organizations use the technology in critical business applications.

    The report found that 35% of surveyed organizations have deployed AI agents capable of taking actions within business applications. However, only 11% of organizations using AI said their governance and security controls were keeping pace with deployment.

    Delinea also found gaps in centralized visibility into agent deployment and permissions, including who owns agents and who approved their use.

    Some respondents reported segregation-of-duties conflicts involving AI, while others identified agents that continued operating after the employees who deployed them had left the organization.

    In a recent development, the research also highlighted gaps in monitoring access across business systems. Only 46% of respondents said they continuously monitor and manage cumulative access risks across applications.

    Those gaps can make it difficult to identify segregation-of-duties conflicts, in which a person or agent has permissions across systems that should be kept separate.

    Despite those challenges, 95% of respondents remarked they were confident their access controls would withstand scrutiny in an external audit.

    However, 26% reported access-related audit findings that had recurred in consecutive years, while 25% said some findings had remained unresolved for three or more years.

    Only 22% of organizations had a single named owner for each application, with ownership tracked in one system of record.

    Meanwhile, 60% reported an increase over the past two years in the number of critical applications operating outside the scope of access governance or Sarbanes-Oxley Act compliance.

    The findings highlight the oversight challenges associated with giving AI agents authority to act within business systems, particularly when organizations cannot consistently identify who owns an agent or trace its actions.

    Frank Vukovits, chief security scientist at Delinea, said organizations remain responsible for the actions AI agents take within their systems.

    According to recent reports, "When an agent can approve a transaction or change permissions, the business owns the outcome. You need to know what every agent can do, who owns it, and who approved it, before an auditor asks or your financials are misstated," Vukovits stated.

    For the full report, go to the Delinea site.

    AI is changing which human capabilities matter most at work, yet employees are reporting that some of those same capabilities are being eroded, according to a new study from IBM.

    OpenAI has declared what it says is an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems, while Anthropic has reported separate advances in research mathematics and formal proof generation.

    Cybersecurity companies Rubrik and CrowdStrike have revealed an expanded identity-security integration designed to move compromised identity environments from threat detection through clean recovery with less manual intervention.

    Increasingly, cyber criminals are sharing AI prompts, jailbreak techniques, and access to existing models that can be incorporated into fraud and phishing operations, according the latest AI Threat Report from Flashpoint.

    📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (595 w)

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Report: Cyber Criminals Move Toward More Targeted Phishing Attacks

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cyber criminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, increasingly using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a latest report from KnowBe4.
    • The company's Phishing Threat Trends Report, Vol.
    • Rather than sending the same fraudulent message to thousands of people, criminals are spending more time researching their targets and creating convincing messages that appear to come from trusted coworkers, businesses, and technology platforms.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cyber criminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, increasingly using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a latest report from KnowBe4. The security firm found that spear-phishing attacks increased 41% over the past year.

    The company's Phishing Threat Trends Report, Vol. 8 found that overall phishing volume increased 29.8% year over year. Organizations received an average of one dangerous e-mail for every 733 messages, but the bigger concern is how attackers are changing their approach.

    Rather than sending the same fraudulent message to thousands of people, criminals are spending more time researching their targets and creating convincing messages that appear to come from trusted coworkers, businesses, and technology platforms.

    The findings are based on threat data from KnowBe4 Defend, the organization's inbound e-mail security platform, which processes approximately 1.15 billion event signals daily.

    KnowBe4 found that several traditional phishing methods declined significantly compared with 2025. Mobile-focused scams dropped 47.3%, advance-fee fraud fell 31.3%, and missed-message scams declined 11.3%.

    Meanwhile, spear phishing increased 41.1%, pre-attack reconnaissance rose 33.7%, and company impersonation climbed 28%.

    The shift suggests that attackers are finding more value in carefully crafted scams that exploit existing business relationships and workplace routines.

    In a recent development, business e-mail compromise (BEC) remains particularly common, accounting for 51.2% of phishing e-mails analyzed in the report. Human resources, finance departments, and executive leadership are among the most frequently targeted groups.

    Attackers also appear to be timing their campaigns around normal business activity. KnowBe4 found that 90.4% of phishing messages arrive Monday through Friday, with Monday accounting for the largest share at 20.6%.

    One of the report's more troubling findings involves the growing use of legitimate technology platforms to deliver malicious content.

    KnowBe4 found that phishing attacks were twice as likely to originate from legitimate infrastructure in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter.

    In a recent development, that includes AI services, where attackers are taking advantage of trusted domains to host fake developer consoles, login prompts, and credential-stealing pages. The report also identified a 228% increase in AI-brand impersonation attacks between March and August.

    Because these malicious pages can operate on legitimate domains with valid security certificates, people may not see the usual warning signs associated with suspicious websites.

    "For years, security advice has focused on a predictable checklist: Check the sender address, hover over the link, and look for the padlock," mentioned Jack Chapman, senior vice president of threat intelligence at KnowBe4.

    "While still foundational, that guidance is becoming less useful by the day.".

    Industry observers note that the findings echo a recent report about management software and AI e-mail assistants. Research from Fortra and Barracuda demonstrated how criminals are using legitimate administrative tools and hidden AI instructions to manipulate users and compromise systems.

    AI is changing which human capabilities matter most at work, yet employees are reporting that some of those same capabilities are being eroded, according to a new study from IBM.

    OpenAI has announced what it says is an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems, while Anthropic has reported separate advances in research mathematics and formal proof generation.

    Cybersecurity companies Rubrik and CrowdStrike have revealed an expanded identity-security integration designed to move compromised identity environments from threat detection through clean recovery with less manual intervention.

    Increasingly, cyber criminals are sharing AI prompts, jailbreak techniques, and access to existing models that can be incorporated into fraud and phishing operations, according the latest AI Threat Report from Flashpoint.

    #123605. The Biggest Spring 2027 Trends Celebrate Glamour and Individual Style

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1227 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

    The Biggest Spring 2027 Trends Celebrate Glamour and Individual Style

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1227 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The breakout trends from the Spring 2027 highlights were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you.
    • There was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere.
    • According to recent reports, and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The breakout trends from the Spring 2027 highlights were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you. From the clashing of statement pieces at Chanel, Dries Van Noten, and Valentino to the coming-out party of the bra at Dior and Altuzarra, the spring runways celebrated self-expression.

    There was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere. Dressing for daytime took on a new sheen via the cummerbunds and opera pumps at Kallmeyer, the metallic gold at Saint Laurent, and the boas at Tory Burch. At Michael Rider’s Celine, utilitarian staples were reimagined in sophisticated silhouettes, while brands like C and Bode took classic straight-leg jeans and added embellishment in the form of sparkle and embroidery. This season was all about celebrating the joy of getting dressed, a principle we think should be applied year-round.

    According to recent reports, and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan. Some were embellished, some had sheer details, and almost all of them fell right below the knee.

    Sources indicate that now that fashion month has wrapped and we’ve had some time to digest what we saw on the runways, we’re rounding up our nine favorite trends from the spring 2027 collections. And because March is still months away, we’ve shopped out some ways to get a jump on the looks now.

    Mixed-and-matched looks were all over the runways. What felt new here was the against-the-grain pattern play, which felt like a message about personal style—an exhortation from designers to stop worrying about following the rules and lean into whatever makes you feel good.

    It has been revealed that this approach allows you to play with things that are already in your wardrobe. Invest in a sparkly skirt to pair with a checkered shirt you already own, or pair a fresh jacquard jacket with some animal-print boots already in your rotation. The key to this trend is making it your own.

    Staud Samira Faux-Fur-Trimmed Jacket.

    Bode Asymmetrical Sequin-Embellished Fringed Skirt.

    Herbert Levine Two-Faced 80 Boot.

    Stripped-back had a whole newly introduced meaning this season! Designers quite literally loosened up a few buttons, exposing delicate bras worn underneath shirting. (Granted, some looks like those at Prada and Tom Ford had just a bra as the top, but we’re going to save that one for warmer months.) What’s so appealing about this look is the contrast between the sexy underpinnings and the polished separates. There’s nothing like a little lace to spice things up, and we are here for it!

    Citizens of Humanity Wool Shirt.

    Gucci Pleated Silk Twill Midi Skirt.

    Borrowing from the boys isn’t newly introduced in fashion. Surely I’m not the only one who loves a Winchester banker shirt with monogrammed initials? But the tuxedo dressing trend—which started on the fall 2026 runways and will be going strong all spring—feels fresh. Designers placed a huge emphasis on the waist (I call it “waistmaxxing”), with the focal point of many looks being the cummerbund. A tuxedo jacket, tailored pants, and opera pumps would create a chic head-to-toe approach, but these pieces look just as cool individually. I love tuxedo pants dressed down with a white T-shirt, for example.

    Zw Collection Stripped Cummerbund Shirt.

    Toccin High-Waisted Tuxedo Trouser.

    It has been revealed that we’ve seen neckerchiefs and bandanas trending in previous seasons, but in spring 2027, neckwear takes a decidedly glam turn with the rise of the feather boa. I loved how Tory Burch paired her boas with car coats and silky shirts with trousers, while Dior’s models wore them with extravagant blazers. Both made the case that these three-dimensional scarves should be worn during the day, which feels cool, unexpected, and very much in keeping with the season’s dressed-up turn.

    The Fresh Arrivals Ilkyaz Ozel Feather Scarf.

    Designers really did their duty this season for the uniform dressers out there. If you love a tonal neutral, there were plenty to choose from in updated silhouettes, from balloon-style cargo pants to work shirts with peplums. What made them feel extra special was the way they were accessorized—with bold, colorful heeled boots and a bright satin bag at Celine, or with neon sandal heels at Balenciaga.

    Co Camo Cotton-Blend Military Jacket.

    JW Anderson Parachute Drawstring Barrel-Leg Track Cargo Pants.

    Sources indicate that the standout jeans this spring are covered in decadent sequins, embroidery, and beading. How fun is that? The key when it comes to styling is keeping your favorite basics on deck and building a look around the jeans. Whether you pair your statement denim with a classic white shirt for work (as seen at Dolce & Gabbana and Bode) or take them for a spin around the town with an equally dazzling top (like at Conner Ives), these are always a good idea—full stop.

    Stella McCartney Crystal Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Embroidered Mid-Rise Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Hellessy Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Ramy Brook Lea Beaded High-Rise Wide-Leg Crop Jeans.

    It has been revealed that with the price of gold at an all-time high and the jewelry market turning to silver, it’s been a refreshing change of pace to see glowing golden hues on the runways. We saw some gold looks sprinkled throughout shows in Fresh York like Ralph Lauren and Fforme, but the collection that really took the medal was Anthony Vaccarello’s final Saint Laurent show, where almost every look had a golden element. From gold jacquard to silky liquid-looking gold tops, these separates can easily spruce up your favorite black trousers for the office or white jeans for a weekend lunch. Or, if you want to take home the trophy, try going head-to-toe gilded for an evening event.

    Dries Van Noten Jacquard Linen, Cotton, and Silk-Blend Coat.

    It’s fair to say that it’s the year of the skirt. Prada may have leaned in hardest, but this classic bottom was all over the runways in every city. The key silhouette was a hybrid pencil/A-line hitting slightly below the knee. (And let me tell you, as a trouser girl, this still sits within my tailored wheelhouse.) There’s a wide range of skirts on the market and an equal range of freedom when it comes to the styling. Whether you pair your skirt with a sweater and loafers for the office or wear it with a sleeveless top and heels for a night out, it’s a piece that can take you just about anywhere.

    Massimo Dutti Pleated Bubble Hem Midi Skirt.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Belted Crinkled Shell-Trimmed Crepe Midi Skirt.

    Marni Black Crinkled Midi Skirt With Daisy Details.

    Simone Rocha Pleated Sheer Satin Midi Skirt.

    Coats aren’t necessarily what most people get excited about in spring—who wants to hide a cute outfit when it’s finally warm enough not to bundle up?—but spring 2027 will be an exception. The coats on the runway this season were much more directional, especially the ones we saw covered in embellishments and jingling and jangling down the catwalk. Next March and April, prepare to layer in pieces that feel equal parts charming and elegant.

    Dries Van Noten Embellished Wool Longline Coat.

    Chan Luu Midnight Studio Coat Black.

    Cinq à Sept Mariella Embellished Faux-Fur-Cuff Coat.

    Prabal Gurung Floral Jacquard Single-Breasted Car Coat.

    • Some families may choose to drop in small gifts every day leading up to Christmas, and some may just hang up stockings as part of their holiday decor—but not fill them up.
    • Sources indicate that we always recommend personalizing each stocking with thoughtful touches tailored to the recipient.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that when we’re shopping for the holidays, we start by thinking about what’s under the tree. But sometimes the coolest gifts are the ones that end up in your stocking. Just because they’re small doesn’t mean they’re not special. That’s why our shopping team set out to find the best stocking stuffer ideas, from the pretty to the practical (and everything in between).

    Some families may choose to drop in small gifts every day leading up to Christmas, and some may just hang up stockings as part of their holiday decor—but not fill them up. Regardless of your approach, everyone knows the best stocking stuffers should be small, thoughtful, useful, and not overly expensive. Think of a candle snuffer, a refreshing room mist, or a bottle stopper that keeps their favorite bottle of wine fresh.

    Sources indicate that we always recommend personalizing each stocking with thoughtful touches tailored to the recipient. Consider what they love to collect, how they spend their free time, or something they’ve mentioned wanting in recent conversations. For homebodies, think cozy socks or candle holders. The BookTok obsessive in your life will love a set of bookmarks with iconic Frank Lloyd Wright designs. If they’re foodies, surprise them with a sardine-themed mouse pad or eye mask set. When it comes to stocking stuffers, the options are endless—and we’ve rounded up over 30 brilliant ideas to help you get started.

    Industry observers note that the bookworm in your life will be so thankful for this gift. The set of magnetic bookmarks keeps their spot after late-night reading, without risk of falling out. And if they have a design eye, they’ll love the geometric motifs from Frank Lloyd Wright.

    Nothing’s quite as awkward as forgetting an anniversary or birthday. This mini journal will save you from that cringe. It goes day-by-day throughout the year, so you can note all of the meaningful dates in your calendar.

    A good candle snuffer is not a want, but a need. It’s so much neater than dipping the wick or just blowing it out. And this adorable one is the (literal) cherry on top. We recommend pairing it with a gourmand-heavy candle.

    Don’t worry, these eye masks from the tinned fish brand Fishwife don’t smell like sardines. Instead, they’re just shaped like adorable fish. They’re reusable, so you can make your everyday eye serum feel like a hands-free spa treatment.

    Sources indicate that anyone who needs a boost of assurance and support this holiday season will appreciate this mirror decal. It’s designed to guide you through anxious moments, and it’s repositionable. So you can see it on your bathroom mirror before bed, or carry the reminder with you on your water bottle.

    Industry observers note that we know a high-quality olive oil can make a great hostess gift, but what if it ended up in your stocking, too? This 1.7-ounce bottle of extra virgin olive oil was harvested from Flamingo Estate’s unique olive trees, and it’s just tiny enough for easy travel.

    It has been revealed that this is way more chic than the matchbooks they pick up at restaurants. You can choose between three engraving/color combos, and it’s the ideal coffee table accessory. This metallic matchbox also comes with a tassel for extra elegance.

    Sources indicate that can one ever have too many trinket dishes? We don’t think so. This one is heartfelt enough for a partner or loved one you want to treasure, and its design is reflective of the English transferware every antique lover is hunting for.

    Industry observers note that level up your next bottle of Cabernet with this aerator and pourer insert. Simply insert this into the bottle opening, and it’ll unlock the fullness of the wine, exposing your giftee to new flavors and ensuring a neat pour.

    Or, if you prefer your drinks bubbly, this glass bottle stopper will keep your prosecco crisp until you’re ready to polish off the bottle. It comes in burnt orange ombré that you’ll reach for again and again.

    It has been revealed that the New Savant is a favorite candle brand of Associate Shopping Editor Janae McKenzie, and their team just released a line of room mists. “Architect’s Daughter smells like the most refreshing library—grapefruit, wood, and eraser shavings that never fail to put me in a creative mood,” McKenzie claims.

    If there’s one person in your life running the holiday baking, say thank you with this cheeky reusable tote. It resembles the butter wrapper they’ve undoubtedly gone through plenty of, and it packs down to run with them on all the last-minute store trips.

    A striking votive holder can make even the most basic tea light candles feel extra special. This mini one from Jonathan Adler is covered in his sculptural Muse D’Or faces, with a gold interior that’ll catch the flame beautifully.

    Recent findings suggest that this is no gas station car freshener. For one, it looks much more elegant. “I gifted my dad one of these years back, and he still raves about them,” McKenzie states. “It doesn’t ruin the look of this car, but it keeps the smell at bay from riding around with our family dog.”.

    This is the dream stocking stuffer for your friend who likes to hike. It’s small enough to tuck in their backpack, but powerful enough to replace binoculars and telescopes. They’ll love birdwatching with this.

    In a recent development, cozy Earth's plush lounge socks feel like pillows for your feet. “I got one of their three packs with solid colors and was surprised by how insanely soft and warm they are,” Senior Commerce Editor Marina Liao says. “They don't make your feet sweat, they don't feel tight and leave marks around your ankles, and they feel exactly like my Guest in Residence cashmere socks, but hold up way better in the wash because they don't actually shrink!”.

    Recent findings suggest that wintertime calls for gearing up in hats, scarves, and gloves, so if you know they could use a nice, warm pair, go with Quince's beloved cashmere-lined leather gloves. They come in brown and black, with touchscreen-friendly fingertips.

    Recent findings suggest that no one can do it all, so if you split the chores with a roommate or partner, this is the perfect small item to drop into their stocking as a nod to your symbiotic relationship. The spoon rest is handmade in Arizona and is just over five inches wide.

    Minted has such an excellent selection of personalized stationery that looks and feels expensive. If they love writing personalized notes and believe in a slower approach to life, they'll want these "snail mail" motif cards in their Christmas stocking.

    📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (449 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Study: Sign-In Problems Are Primary Drivers of Help Desk Tickets

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a newly introduced study from ControlUp.
    • Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations company identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) issues as major drivers of support demand.
    • It has been revealed that at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a newly introduced study from ControlUp.

    Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations company identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) issues as major drivers of support demand.

    It has been revealed that at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems. Meanwhile, 87% of network and phone tickets were reassigned between teams, compared with 20% of account tickets.

    It has been revealed that MFA enrollment and re-enrollment problems appeared at 40% of organizations, with one in five linking these issues to employees replacing or upgrading their phones. Virtual desktop problems appeared at 55% of organizations analyzed.

    Traditional phone support remained a major channel for IT assistance.

    It has been revealed that among organizations that recorded how support requests were submitted, 57% reported that phone calls accounted for approximately two-thirds or more of contacts. At one organization, that figure reached 99%.

    It has been revealed that machine-generated tickets from monitoring, security, backup, and patching systems appeared at half of the organizations studied. At 15%, automated tickets represented between 25% and 50% of all requests.

    The research covered enterprises across retail, healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, construction, energy, and IT services.

    ControlUp said the findings highlight the need to evaluate recurring problems and their operational impact rather than relying solely on ticket volume and resolution speed.

    "IT organizations have traditionally measured support performance by how promptly they close tickets, but that doesn't tell the whole story," stated Simon Townsend, senior vice president of marketing and office of the CTO at ControlUp.

    "A password reset that takes a few minutes and an infrastructure failure that disrupts an entire location shouldn't carry the same operational weight.".

    For more information, go to the ControlUp site.

    OpenAI has announced what it says is an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems, while Anthropic has reported separate advances in research mathematics and formal proof generation.

    Cybersecurity companies Rubrik and CrowdStrike have unveiled an expanded identity-security integration designed to move compromised identity environments from threat detection through clean recovery with less manual intervention.

    Increasingly, cyber criminals are sharing AI prompts, jailbreak techniques, and access to existing models that can be incorporated into fraud and phishing operations, according the latest AI Threat Report from Flashpoint.

    #123601. Tech Report: Van Cleef & Arpels Explores the Secrets and Mysteries of Ancient Egypt

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1109 w)

    Tech Report: Van Cleef & Arpels Explores the Secrets and Mysteries of Ancient Egypt

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1109 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After archaeologist Howard Carter and his team discovered King Tutankhamun’s tomb in 1922, regal diadems, golden collars, and bold cuffs brought a fresh wave of Egyptian Revival into the Art Deco movement.
    • From opulent collars to sculptural rings, each design harkens back to the arts, values, and beliefs that defined the Newly introduced Kingdom.
    • Industry observers note that “There are a lot of real animals that were fashioned into amulets and small statues, likely to imbue the owners with some of their traits, but also to revere the creature and the benefits it provided,” archaeologist Randall Hixenbaugh tells Bazaar.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After archaeologist Howard Carter and his team discovered King Tutankhamun’s tomb in 1922, regal diadems, golden collars, and bold cuffs brought a fresh wave of Egyptian Revival into the Art Deco movement. Van Cleef & Arpels took note and added Egyptian-inspired calligraphy, hieroglyphs, and semiprecious stones into its lexicon of deco bracelets, sautoirs, and brooches, bringing a historic feel to the frostbitten glamour that defined the roaring ’20s. Now, over a century later, the maison’s new Fascinating Egypt high jewelry collection explores more avenues of the region’s mystical splendor.

    From opulent collars to sculptural rings, each design harkens back to the arts, values, and beliefs that defined the Newly introduced Kingdom. But just as Egyptologists explored hidden messages beneath the grandeur of the 18th dynasty, Van Cleef conveys the mystique beneath its history. Shape-shifting necklaces function like secret passageways to new realms of expression, and Mysterioux brooches reincarnate sacred deities in gold and gemstones. Just take the Bennou, a terrestrial vessel for the sun god Ra, whose feathers of emeralds, marine-blue sapphires, lapis, cerulean slips of turquoise, mother of pearl, and drops of diamonds represent the colors of the earth. A blood-orange spessartite garnet with rays of diamonds hangs from a red spinel, like a drop of sunshine.

    Industry observers note that “There are a lot of real animals that were fashioned into amulets and small statues, likely to imbue the owners with some of their traits, but also to revere the creature and the benefits it provided,” archaeologist Randall Hixenbaugh tells Bazaar. His namesake gallery in Manhattan’s Design District is home to artifacts sourced in accordance with the ethical standards set by the International Association of Dealers in Ancient Arts.

    Talismans were worn like supplements to enhance the human experience—cats to spark joy, mongooses to offer protection from snakes, and frogs for fertility. Stones of certain colors were valued for their connotations with abundance and immortality. “The Egyptians prized bright blue and green materials, which were associated with the Nile, the sky, and life itself. Lapis lazuli was rare and valuable and therefore associated with the pharaohs. Its extensive use on King Tut’s gold mask demonstrates how highly regarded it was,” Hixenbaugh explains.

    The cobalt stone finds its way into all kinds of Van Cleef’s latest creations. It’s used generously in the “Ornement de Saphir” necklace, whose central totem resembles an evil eye, with an oval-cut sapphire pupil plopped cleverly in an iris of pavé diamonds. Suspended from a panel of lapis lazuli interspersed with slivers of gold and baguette-cut rubies, the pendant is detachable and can be worn like a brooch, while its Corde chain incorporates clasps concealed beneath colorful rondelles that allow it to transform into a pair of bracelets. A concept conceived in the 1940s, the versatile signature speaks to the ongoing conversation between the house’s heritage and Egypt’s mystique.

    Some of Van Cleef’s most striking interpretations of the ancient kingdom come through in Art Deco bracelets. The articulated cuff style was a staple of the 1920s, with ample real estate for planes of illustrious motifs to flourish. Instead of a painter’s palette, Van Cleef brought diamonds, emeralds, and rubies together like dots on a pointillist painting through the “mystery set” technique (a manner of setting gemstones sans prongs).

    In a recent development, the house patented the method in the 1930s and has continued to enlist it to craft seamless gemscapes, extending into a series of “Paysage” bracelets. Clad in fields of gemstones, the deco-style pieces bring Egyptian royals, celestial skies, and monuments to life. Openwork, a technique that minimizes the use of solid metals, enables light to pass through each bejeweled mural, amplifying the high shine of each cuff. Other inconspicuous elements, like golden hieroglyphic nuggets, rest beneath articulated columns, like artifacts awaiting discovery.

    The house’s bold fonts of design can be equally understood through the juxtaposition of lolly-like cabochons and sugar-white diamonds. Amid the sea of platinum and flashy Asscher cuts that defined Gatsby-era decadence, Van Cleef & Arpels brought teardrop emeralds into the mix. Suspended from pillars of diamonds set in platinum, the plump stones hung like enticing lozenges throughout a collaret necklace, circa 1929. The spellbinding masterpiece drew the eye of Egyptian royalty, Her Royal Highness Princess Faiza, who purchased the necklace in 1937. It was a convergence of brilliant facets and vivid, dome-shaped gems that bridged the gradual shift into midcentury modern shapes and matte stones. The provenance of the design influenced the maison’s updated rendition of the crown jewel, featuring luscious emeralds and slender pearls suspended from elongated pendants of white gold and diamonds.

    Recent findings suggest that by the 1950s, Van Cleef’s interpretations of Egyptomania embraced organic forms, space-age ellipses, and plots of semiprecious stones. Smooth, matte surfaces of turquoise, malachite, and coral enhanced the realism of biomorphic designs, like a scarab clip with wings of turquoise, circa 1957. (The house would lend the brooch to the Petit Palais for the debut of “Tutankhamun and His Time” nearly a decade later.) Such vibrant stones extended into contemporary aesthetics of the 1980s, such as a collar necklace slathered in slices of jade, stripes of onyx, and birds carved out of coral.

    Industry observers note that this collection revisited the era through the language of Ettore Sottsass and the Memphis Group, a 1980s decorative arts firm, for spherical shapes and elements of cubism to take flight. Some of Sottsass’s most recognizable pieces include a sterling silver fruit stand with zigzag pillars and a colorblocked bookstand named “The Carlton.” Van Cleef translates this friction between elements smooth and sharp, glossy and matte into pieces like a saucer-shaped Mythe Celeste clip, coated in sheets of lapis and malachite with buttons of coral—elements beheld by the Egyptians as modalities of abundance and immortality. By contrast, a Frise Divine ring juxtaposes an oval-shaped Sri Lankan sapphire with a rigid tile of coral, and rows of diamonds set in zigzag streams of gold.

    Sources indicate that all creations in the Fascinating Egypt œuvre are united by tradition, a preservation of heritage echoed in the foundations of other art forms, like ballet. In fact, the house’s seamless dances of emeralds, rubies, and diamonds compelled George Balanchine to choreograph Jewels for the Upcoming York City Ballet in 1931—a moment that came full circle when the jewelers debuted a collection of ballerina clips and brooches a couple of years later. The nature of their anatomically sound arms, gilded in gold and ribbons of gemstones, extends into the collection’s Muse Éternelle brooches. Modeled after Cleopatra, the palm-sized figures are enrobed in a variety of dazzling threads of gold, strewn with diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and emeralds.

    Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.
    • In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025.
    • A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

    A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

    Recent findings suggest that menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

    The report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

    Industry observers note that the practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

    "Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao said in the firm's announcement.

    Sources indicate that menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

    An agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

    Menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

    In a recent development, the report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

    Sources indicate that A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG indicates ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

    That provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

    For enterprise leaders, the new spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

    Menlo's State of Enterprise AI report is available here.
